end.summary:
Mahi practised that a freely suspended magnet settles roughly north–south; this still needs checking for consistency.
Mahi practised using a compass to find directions; this still needs checking next time.
Mahi identified Earth as a large magnet and linked the needle’s movement to magnetic pull.
The idea that cold makes a compass point north was still present at the end and was not corrected after the last mention.
end.parentNote: Asha practised finding directions with Mahi using a magnet and compass. Mahi connected the compass needle with Earth’s magnetic effect and noticed that nearby magnets can change the needle’s direction. The cold-weather explanation came up again at the end, so it still needs revisiting; using a simple compass-and-magnet demonstration at home, away from metal objects, may help.
